title: Add glossy wet-plate shine effect to 3D plate components
description: Add more gloss, shine, and specular highlights to the 3D plate sections and base to create a wet/glazed plate effect. This should increase visual contrast between lit and shadowed areas. Also adjust directional lighting angle to cast better shadows on plate edges for more visible depth. Consider adding subtle environment reflections or specular smudge artifacts across surfaces.
close_reason: Added glossy wet-plate materials with clearcoat and improved lighting

title: Add mouse-tracking rotation to plate cards via GSAP
description: When mouse is inside a LazyPlate card, the 3D plate rotates on Y-axis tracking horizontal mouse position. Total rotation range ~120-160°. Gives a parallax-like feel as mouse moves left to right. Uses GSAP for smooth interpolation. Especially impactful on the 5-section Premium plate.

title: Create GSAP entrance animation for plate in builder screen
description: Investigate and implement a visually impressive entrance animation when the LazyPlateBuilder opens. Research good 3D reveal/entrance patterns (spin-in, stagger sections, scale-up with bounce, etc). Use GSAP for orchestration. Will likely need iteration to find the right feel. Consider: sections flying in one-by-one, plate scaling up with overshoot, rotation flourish, particle burst, etc.

title: Add 3D plate visual to LazyPlateBuilder bottom sheet
description: When you tap 'Build Yours' on a Lazy Plate card, the LazyPlateBuilder bottom sheet opens but has no plate visual — just step dots and a list of choices. Add the 3D MenuPie plate to the builder sheet header area so users see their plate being assembled as they pick items. The plate should update reactively: as each step is completed, the corresponding pie section should visually fill/highlight. Depends on Fortwoks.Site-zg5 (configurable sections) so the Premium 5-section plate renders correctly in the builder.

title: 3D plate visual aesthetic needs redesign
description:
The current 3D plate rendering has good technical dynamics (contrast, specular highlights) but the overall aesthetic isn't working. 

Current issues:
- Lighting setup doesn't create the right mood/feel
- Colors aren't translating well from the button accents to the 3D materials
- The glossy material + current light setup creates a look that doesn't match the brand

Need to rethink:
- Overall lighting approach (maybe warmer/cooler tones?)
- How accent colors are applied to materials
- The entire visual language of the plates

Original request that got lost: wanted a dramatic camera angle (like looking down the barrel of a gun, camera at top-right looking down-left) with sections that really pop when active. Current camera system doesn't support the rotation needed for this.

title: Plate rotation not having expected visual impact
description:
Added plate rotation support (70° Z-axis, 30° Y-axis anti-clockwise) but the visual change is minimal and not creating the dramatic side-on barrel effect expected.

Current implementation:
- Added plateRotation to plate-config.ts
- Applied rotation to both plateGroup and sectionsGroup in PlateScene
- Rotation values: z: -70°, y: -30°

The rotation is technically being applied (can see slight tilt in modal) but it's not producing the dramatic angle change we need.

Potential issues:
- Rotation order (Euler angle gimbal lock?)
- Camera position/FOV might be fighting the rotation
- Need to rotate about a different origin point?
- May need to transform the entire scene coordinate system differently

Need to:
1. Understand Three.js rotation mechanics better
2. Experiment with different rotation approaches
3. Possibly add rotation visualization/debugging tools
4. Consider if we need to rotate camera instead of/in addition to plate

Related: Fortwoks.Site-787 (aesthetic redesign)

title: Rotate plate to selected section on selection
description: When a section is selected/active, the plate should rotate to bring that section to the front/center. For the 2-section Saver plate, this means rotating ~160 degrees for the second section. For the 5-section Premium plate, each section should step by its angular width (72 degrees per section). Add a stepping config per plate that maps each section index to a rotation amount. This rotation should be toggleable on/off via config. Use GSAP for smooth animated transitions.
close_reason: Added section-aware rotation with GSAP stepping per plate type

title: Add explosive burst effect on section selection
description: When a plate section becomes active (selected in builder), add a particle burst / shockwave / radial flash effect around the section to make the activation feel explosive and impactful. Investigate options: particle emitter ring, expanding glow ring, shockwave distortion, starburst rays. Use GSAP for orchestration. Should complement the existing lift + emissive glow, not replace it.

title: Resize plate configurator for card layout
description: The plate configurator canvas currently uses camera settings (fov: 32, position: [3.5, 2.6, 4]) designed for a full-viewport display. For the MenuCard component at ~280px height, the plate appears slightly squeezed. Adjust plateConfig camera values and possibly plate radius/float height to frame the plate better at card size. Consider adding a 'compact' config variant that MenuCard can pass to PlateScene.

title: Add hover-highlight effect to individual plate sections
description: When hovering over a pie section, it raises up slightly and glows more (emissive increase). All other sections stay in default state. Critical for the LazyPlateBuilder flow where it provides selection feedback — lights up the active section. May be disabled on the main menu cards. Uses GSAP for smooth raise/glow transitions.

title: Highlighted plate section changes color incorrectly due to lighting
description: When a plate section is highlighted/active, the emissive lighting approach changes the color in an undesirable way. Instead of using emissive multipliers, switch to a brighter base color for the active state. The highlighted section should appear as a brighter, more vivid version of its base color rather than a washed-out emissive glow.
close_reason: Fixed highlight to use brighter base color instead of emissive wash

title: Fix plate configurator rendering glitch
description: The 3D plate scene has a constant visual glitch/flicker. Likely caused by mixing Svelte 4 reactive statements ($:) with Svelte 5 runes in PlateScene.svelte and PieSection.svelte. The $: mainActive and $: sideActive bindings plus the $: emissiveIntensity patterns may be causing reactivity conflicts and re-render thrashing. Migrate all components to pure Svelte 5 runes ($derived, $props).

title: Make 3D plate sections configurable (count, angles, animation)
description: PlateScene currently hardcodes 2 sections (main 216deg + side 144deg) via plate-config.ts. Make it accept a dynamic section count and per-section degree allocation so the same component renders both the Saver (2-section) and Premium (5-section) plates. Key changes: PlateScene needs a sections prop (array of {startDeg, endDeg, floorColor, rimColor}), pie-renderer utils need to generate N clip plane sets dynamically, and the animation loop needs to sync all N sets. MenuPie should pass this through so the LazyPlatesSection plateVisual snippet can differentiate per plate.sections count.
